motivo: Todas las afirmaciones fácticas coinciden con páginas de NWS (Binghamton 'Weather in Action: Downburst', glosario NWS de outflow boundary, páginas NWS de heat bursts). No hay cifras ni unidades en el guion ni en el caption. Ninguna frase es dudosa o falsa; no hay salud/seguridad/plata. La atribución 'The National Weather Service compares it to...' es correcta. Observación menor, no bloqueante: la página NWS Sioux Falls de heat burst no dice explícitamente 'rare'; la frase usa 'every once in a while', compatible con fuentes que lo describen como raro.

afirmaciones.texto: The storm ends and, all of a sudden, it's cooler.
afirmaciones.fuente: https://www.weather.gov/bgm/WeatherInActionDownburst ; glosario NWS outflow boundary ('passage marked by a wind shift and usually a drop in temperature')

afirmaciones.texto: The rain brought it. / Inside the cloud, raindrops evaporate, and evaporating pulls heat out of the air.
afirmaciones.fuente: NWS Binghamton: 'air within the thunderstorm is rapidly cooled by evaporating raindrops'

afirmaciones.texto: That cooled air is heavier than the air around it, so it sinks toward the ground.
afirmaciones.fuente: NWS Binghamton: 'Since cold air is more dense than warm air, this rain-cooled air begins to descend toward the ground.' (heavier = más densa)

afirmaciones.texto: The National Weather Service compares it to a glass of water spilled on pavement: when it hits the ground, it spreads out in every direction.
afirmaciones.fuente: NWS Binghamton: 'it moves out in all directions much like a glass of water that is spilled on pavement.'

afirmaciones.texto: So it's, more or less, a cold front in miniature. / In its glossary, the NWS says that edge of cool air has an effect similar to a cold front.
afirmaciones.fuente: Glosario NWS: outflow boundary, 'similar in effect to a cold front, with passage marked by a wind shift and usually a drop in temperature' (https://www.weather.gov/spotterguide/glossary_o)

afirmaciones.texto: Heads up: not always. Every once in a while, the air coming down arrives hot. / (it's called a 'heat burst')
afirmaciones.fuente: NWS Sioux Falls https://www.weather.gov/fsd/20170516-heatburst-nwiaswmn (aire descendente 'warmer and drier' que el aire previo a la tormenta); NWS Des Moines y SKYbrary describen el fenómeno como raro

afirmaciones.texto: Caption: Send this to the friend who steps outside and says 'finally, it cooled off.' / línea de Sources
afirmaciones.fuente: No es afirmación fáctica (llamado a la acción); la lista de fuentes coincide con las páginas consultadas
